transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. I'd like to call this approval meeting to order. As we know, we have a draft notification package related to the cloud security incident that needs to be finalized this week, including the regulatory filing and customer notices. Before I can give my final approval, per our incident-response protocol, I need each responsible counsel from the participating functions to report their relevant findings. Let's start with whoever is ready to present their function's findings.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to report a critical finding from my review of the cloud-access logs. I confirmed that exactly 2,736 accounts had both names and email addresses exposed together with unencrypted Social Security numbers. I want to flag that the preliminary incident summary still lists the record count as undetermined because the forensic reconciliation was completed after that summary circulated. This updated count needs to be reflected in the notification package and regulatory filing before approval.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I have a critical finding from my review on the regulatory filing side. I checked the current state regulator incident portal and confirmed that for this incident's data elements, the Massachusetts Attorney General filing must be submitted no later than the same day as the consumer notices. The filing sequence is currently absent from the draft package because the portal instruction changed this month. This needs to be addressed before the package is approved and released.

transcript.text: I have a critical finding from my review on the insurance side. I reviewed the cyber policy endorsement and confirmed that written insurer consent is required before the company promises identity-restoration services or other remediation benefits to affected customers. I received the endorsement amendment from the broker yesterday but have not yet added it to the notification checklist. If the customer notices include any promises of identity-restoration or remediation benefits, we need to obtain written insurer consent before the package is approved and released.

transcript.text: I have a critical finding from my review on the client relations side. I confirmed in a call with the client relationship executive that the client has authorized 24 months of identity-restoration services and requires the customer notice to state that the company is not admitting negligence. These instructions were given after the draft notice was prepared, so the current draft does not yet reflect either of these requirements. The 24-month identity-restoration commitment is relevant to Marcus's insurance finding -- the customer notices will include identity-restoration promises, so written insurer consent will be needed. And the no-negligence language must be added to the customer notices before the package is approved and released.

Ensure the Massachusetts Attorney General filing is submitted no later than the same day as the consumer notices, and document the filing sequence in the package.
Obtain written insurer consent before the customer notices promise identity-restoration or remediation benefits, per the policy endorsement.
Add the 24-month identity-restoration services commitment and the no-negligence language to the customer notices before release.
